data.howToName: How to scale a recipe from 4 servings to 10
notes: 2.5 times the leavening is too much. Use about 2 times.
Salt and spices: start at about 2 times, then taste.
Check the pan size. 2.5 times the food needs a bigger pot or two pans.

description: Scale a recipe that serves 4 up to 10 servings. The factor is 2.5, so every amount is multiplied by 2.5, with fractions rounded to measurable amounts.

examples.result: The scaled curry serves 10: 5 cups chicken, 2 1/2 cups sauce, 5 cloves garlic, 5 teaspoons spice mix.
steps: Multiply each amount by 2.5: 2 cups chicken become 5 cups, 1 cup sauce becomes 2 1/2 cups.
Garlic: 2 cloves × 2.5 = 5 cloves. Spice mix: 2 teaspoons × 2.5 = 5 teaspoons.
examples.title: A curry for 4, scaled to serve 10

examples.result: The scaled cake uses 5 cups flour, 2 1/2 cups sugar, 5 eggs, and 2 teaspoons baking powder.
steps: Flour: 2 cups × 2.5 = 5 cups. Sugar: 1 cup × 2.5 = 2 1/2 cups. Eggs: 2 × 2.5 = 5.
Baking powder is the exception: 1 teaspoon × 2 = 2 teaspoons, not 2 1/2.
examples.title: A cake for 4, scaled to serve 10

faqs.answer: Divide the servings you want by the servings the recipe makes: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. Multiply every ingredient by 2.5. The scaler above does it one ingredient at a time.
faqs.question: What is the scale factor from 4 servings to 10?

faqs.answer: Round to the nearest eighth of a cup, which is what the scaler does. 1/3 cup times 2.5 is 5/6 of a cup, which rounds to 7/8 of a cup, or 14 tablespoons. For baking, weighing in grams is cleaner than rounding cups.
faqs.question: How do I measure awkward amounts like 5/6 of a cup?

faqs.answer: No. Use about 2 times the leavening rather than 2.5 times. The common rule of thumb is about three-quarters of the linear amount when scaling up, and 2 is close to three-quarters of 2.5.
faqs.question: Do I multiply the baking powder by 2.5 too?

faqs.answer: A recipe for 4 stretched to 10 is two and a half times the food, so the pot or pan needs to be two and a half times the size. If it does not fit, cook in two batches. A crowded pan steams instead of browning.
faqs.question: What size pot do I need for 10 servings?

faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the most common version of it: a recipe written for a family of 4, cooked for a table of 10. Dinner parties, holiday meals, and big family weekends all land on this scaling.
faqs.question: Is 4 to 10 a common scaling?

faqs.answer: Yes. 2.5 is not a neat doubling, so write the scaled list down before you start. Guessing amounts halfway through cooking is how a good recipe goes wrong.
faqs.question: Should I write the scaled amounts down first?

felicityNote: Four to ten is my dinner party scaling. The recipe says four, the table says ten, and the factor of 2.5 is the number I reach for most.

parts.meaning: The multiplier for every ingredient. From 4 to 10 servings, the factor is 2.5.
The number of servings you want to make. Here, 10.
The number of servings the recipe makes as written. Here, 4.
The amount of one ingredient after scaling.

formula.text: Scale factor = desired servings ÷ original servings. Scaled amount = original amount × scale factor. From 4 to 10 servings, the factor is 2.5.

howToSteps.name: Find the factor
howToSteps.text: Divide the servings you want by the servings the recipe makes. 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.

howToSteps.name: Multiply everything by 2.5
howToSteps.text: Work down the ingredient list and multiply each amount by 2.5. Round cups to the nearest eighth, or weigh in grams.

howToSteps.name: Hold back the leavening
howToSteps.text: Baking powder, baking soda, and yeast get about 2 times, not 2.5 times. Too much leavening makes bakes rise fast and sink.

howToSteps.name: Season in stages
howToSteps.text: Start salt and strong spices at about 2 times, then taste and add more. Big batches are easy to overseason.

howToSteps.name: Check the pot
howToSteps.text: Two and a half times the food needs a much bigger pot or pan. If it does not fit comfortably, cook in two batches.

lede: A recipe for 4 stretched to 10 has a scale factor of 2.5. Multiply every ingredient by 2.5 and round to the nearest eighth of a cup.

title: Scale a Recipe from 4 Servings to 10
tutorial: Four to ten is the dinner party scaling. Most recipes serve four, and a dinner party is rarely four people. The factor is 2.5: 10 divided by 4. Every ingredient gets multiplied by 2.5, which is easy maths for the big amounts and awkward maths for the small ones. One cup becomes 2 1/2 cups. A third of a cup becomes 5/6 of a cup, which rounds to 7/8, or 14 tablespoons. The scaler above rounds cups to the nearest eighth, so the answers stay measurable.

Weighing is the cleaner option at this factor. Two hundred grams times 2.5 is 500 g, exactly. A third of a cup times 2.5 is a fraction nobody can measure. If the recipe gives cups and you have a scale, convert the cups to grams first, then scale. The numbers stay exact, and baking especially rewards the precision. A large egg is about 50 g out of the shell, so 2 eggs scaled to 5 is about 250 g, which is easy to check on the scale.

Leavening needs the usual holdback. At a factor of 2.5, the linear amount of baking powder would be 2 1/2 times the original, and that is too much. The common rule of thumb is about three-quarters of the linear amount when scaling up, which lands near 2 times here. Use about double the baking powder or soda, not two and a half times. Salt and strong spices follow the same pattern: start at about 2 times, then taste and add more.

The pot is the practical limit. Two and a half times the food needs a pot two and a half times the size, and a crowded pot steams instead of browning. If the batch does not fit comfortably, cook in two batches rather than cramming it into one. Two batches also give you a second chance: if the first one needs more seasoning, the second one gets it right.

Ten servings almost always means leftovers, even with a hungry table. Plan for them before you cook: have containers ready, cool the extra food quickly, and get it into the fridge the same day. A scaled up dinner party is a gift to your future self, but only if the leftovers are stored properly and eaten within a few days.
